name: Arduino (Arduino S.r.l. / Arduino LLC; Qualcomm deal announced 2025)
subcategory: microcontroller boards, IDE and cloud for makers, education and industry
origin_detail: Begun in 2005 at the Interaction Design Institute Ivrea (Italy) as a fork of Wiring, Hernando Barragan's 2004 master's-thesis platform. Core team: Massimo Banzi, David Cuartielles, Tom Igoe, Gianluca Martino and David Mellis. The five co-founders formed Arduino LLC in early 2008 to hold the trademarks.
flagship_projects: UNO Q with App Lab (2025, Qualcomm Dragonwing QRB2210 + STM32U585)
openness_notes: Hardware column. From the start the reference board designs were published under CC BY-SA 2.5 and the software under GPL/LGPL (the IDE 1.x source is GPL v2; Wikipedia lists AGPL-3.0 for IDE 2.0). That makes it level 3, not 4. Governance has always been corporate, and the Arduino Foundation announced in 2016 was withdrawn. Two closing episodes are on record. In July 2017, CEO Federico Musto reportedly pulled many open-source licences, schematics and code from the website, until the founders' company BCMI bought Arduino AG. Then, after the October 2025 Qualcomm announcement, the Terms of Service revised on 2025-10-29 added a ban on reverse-engineering the Platform and a perpetual, irrevocable, sub-licensable licence over user content. Arduino says the reverse-engineering restriction covers only its SaaS cloud and that 'anything that was open, stays open'. UNO Q Gerber files were released shortly after launch. The level stays 3, but control is moving to the cloud and services layer and to a chip-vendor parent.

Contracting parties are Arduino S.r.l. and, for Premium Services, Arduino LLC. s8.2: no translating, decompiling or reverse-engineering 'the Platform'. s7.1: users grant a non-exclusive, royalty-free, transferable, sub-licensable, perpetual, irrevocable licence over their content. s9.4: Arduino may monitor accounts and use of its AI Products. s3.2: no using the Platform to develop competing services. s8.4: open-source-licensed material is carved out.

relicensing_events.from: Open designs (CC BY-SA), schematics and code published on the website
relicensing_events.to: Many open-source licences, schematics and code reportedly removed from the website
relicensing_events.outcome_note: Under Arduino SRL's CEO Federico Musto, after Wired reported that he had fabricated his academic record. In July 2017 BCMI (Banzi, Cuartielles, Mellis, Igoe) acquired Arduino AG and all the trademarks, and Fabio Violante replaced Musto.

exit_events.note: On 1 Oct 2016 Arduino LLC and Arduino SRL announced a merger into Arduino AG, ending the trademark dispute

exit_events.counterparty: BCMI (company of founders Banzi, Cuartielles, Mellis, Igoe)
exit_events.note: BCMI acquired Arduino AG and all the Arduino trademarks in July 2017

Announced 2025-10-07; price undisclosed. Arduino is to become an independent subsidiary and keep its multi-vendor chips (ST, Renesas, Microchip, NXP). Arduino's announcement said closing was subject to regulatory approval and customary conditions. No primary source confirming the closing date was found; see notes.

risk_events: 2008-2016: trademark split. Gianluca Martino's Smart Projects secretly registered the Arduino trademark in Italy in late 2008. It stopped paying royalties and renamed itself Arduino SRL in 2014. Arduino LLC sued in Jan 2015 and created the Genuino brand in May 2015. A merger into Arduino AG was announced in Oct 2016.

2017: CEO Federico Musto admitted he never earned the degrees he claimed (reported by Wired), and open-source files were reportedly pulled from the website. The founders' company BCMI bought out the company in July 2017.

Clones: about 1 genuine board is sold for every 5-6 clones worldwide, at under half the price. India, the largest market for IDE downloads (3.2M), is under 1% of customers (CEO Fabio Violante, TechCrunch 2023-12-22).
2025-10: the Qualcomm acquisition (price undisclosed) puts a chip vendor in control. UNO Q is the first Arduino board with a Qualcomm chip.

2025-10-29: the new Terms of Service ban reverse-engineering the Platform, take a perpetual, irrevocable licence over user content and allow monitoring of AI use. Community concerns drew Arduino's 2025-11-21 'setting the record straight' post.
robustness: The board designs (CC BY-SA), IDE (GPL/AGPL) and libraries are open and widely copied, so the hardware and toolchain ecosystem could outlive any owner. The brand, Arduino Cloud, App Lab and enterprise lines are company-controlled and now owned by Qualcomm. The Arduino Foundation announced in 2016 was withdrawn, so no neutral governance body exists. Arduino's Nov 2025 Q&A says multi-vendor microcontroller support (ST, Microchip, Renesas) continues.
physical_science_relevance: Arduino is the de facto standard microcontroller platform for low-cost lab instrumentation, sensor readout and DIY automation. An Arduino Uno R3 is part of this lab's CubXL hardware.
openness_effect_assessment: Openness made Arduino the default: about 300,000 official boards by mid-2011, about 700,000 by 2013 and about 30M active IDE users by Feb 2020. The same CC BY-SA designs let clones outsell genuine boards about 5-6 to 1 (2023), which hurts a company whose CEO says revenue comes from selling original hardware. Arduino answered with harder-to-copy, more complex boards and moved into enterprise and cloud, funded by $54M of VC (2022-2023). The asset actually fought over in 2008-2016 was the trademark, not the licence.
key_takeaway: Arduino is the canonical open-hardware success whose value went mostly to the ecosystem and to clone makers rather than to the company. The path runs from academic origin (2005), through a trademark fight that split the brand (2008-2016) and a founder buyback (2017), to modest venture funding ($54M, 2022-2023). It ends in consolidation into a chip vendor: Qualcomm, announced Oct 2025, price undisclosed, closing not confirmed by a primary source here. The published designs have so far stayed open, but the post-announcement Terms of Service (Oct 2025) tightened control of the cloud platform and user content. Openness persisted in the artifacts while control moved to the trademark, the platform and the parent company.

hardware_extras.clone_impacts: About 1 genuine board is sold for every 5-6 clones worldwide, and clones cost under half the price. India, the largest market for IDE downloads (3.2M), is under 1% of customers, which the CEO attributes to fakes. Qualcomm closing is not confirmed by a primary source. Arduino's 2025-10-07 post calls it an agreement subject to regulatory approval. Qualcomm's Wikipedia article lists Arduino as a subsidiary acquired in October 2025. Arduino's 2025-11-21 post refers to 'the Qualcomm acquisition' without saying it closed. The Arduino blog archives for Nov and Dec 2025 (first pages) contain no closing announcement. ownership_status is 'acquired' on that basis and should be checked against Qualcomm's FY2026 10-K.

What changed in the Terms of Service: the current text (last revised 2025-10-29) was read, but the previous version was not, because web.archive.org could not be fetched. The changes listed are the clauses criticised and then explained in Arduino's 2025-11-21 post, not a verified diff.
funding_total_usd is the sum of the two disclosed rounds: the $32M Series B (Jun 2022) and the $22M extension (Sep 2023). Earlier funding, if any, was not found.
No revenue, employee count or valuation was found. The Qualcomm price was undisclosed.

unconfirmed.reason: Deal closing not confirmed by any primary page. Qualcomm's release rendered only its headline ('to Acquire'). Arduino's 2025-10-07 post says 'The closing of this transaction is subject to regulatory approval and other customary closing conditions.' arduino.cc/en/about makes no ownership statement. EDGAR full-text search finds no Qualcomm (CIK 804328) filing since 2025-10-01 mentioning Arduino, and no 10-K/10-Q/8-K mentioning both. Wikipedia's Arduino article says '(now owned by Qualcomm)' but gives no completion date (secondary only).
Only the cited Wikipedia states 2005 ('The Arduino project began in 2005 as a tool for students at the Interaction Design Institute Ivrea'); arduino.cc/en/about gives no year.

verification_pass2.note: The $54M total is Arduino's own figure for its Series B including the 2023 extension, matching the file's sum of the TechCrunch rounds; earlier funding, if any, remains unknown. The 2022-06-07 Arduino post ('Ready to transform the enterprise world? We are!') mentions Bosch, Renesas, Anzu Partners and Arm only as partners in its excerpt, so the $32M figure was not re-found separately. Qualcomm's SEC filings do not mention Arduino (EDGAR full-text search, 0 hits), so the file's suggestion to check Qualcomm's FY2026 10-K is unlikely to settle whether the deal closed. ownership_status 'acquired' still rests on Wikipedia alone. Confidence stays medium because closing is unconfirmed.
